2027-01-13.title: Wednesday after the First Sunday after Denho
readings: Prayers for everyone; one mediator, Christ Jesus
2027-01-13.verse: Why do you see the speck in your neighbor's eye, but do not notice the log in your own eye?
theo: Paul asks Timothy for a Church that prays for everyone: “supplications, prayers, intercessions, and thanksgivings be made for everyone, for kings and all who are in high positions.” Why everyone? Because God “desires everyone to be saved and to come to the knowledge of the truth. For there is one God; there is also one mediator between God and humankind, Christ Jesus, himself human.” The Church's prayer is as wide as God's desire to save.

Jesus forbids the opposite attitude: “Do not judge, so that you may not be judged.” With humour he describes a man with a log in his eye trying to remove a speck from his brother's. This is not a ban on all discernment; it is a ban on condemning, on the harsh eye that sees others' faults and never its own. Intercession and judging cannot live in the same heart: we cannot pray sincerely for someone while condemning him.
outline: Ask: for whom do you find it hard to pray?
Point 3 · The log and the speck
Look first at your own eye.
“Do not judge, so that you may not be judged.”
live: Pray today by name for our national and state leaders.
Before criticising anyone today, name one fault of your own.
2027-01-13.prayer: Lord Jesus, one mediator between God and humankind, you desire all to be saved. Widen my prayer to include everyone, and free me from judging others, so that I may first see my own faults. Amen.
altar: The intercessions of the Holy Qurbono include the whole world: rulers, the sick, travellers, the departed. There we learn to pray for everyone.

quick: Christ is the one mediator; God wants all to be saved.
Do not judge: first remove the log from your own eye.
2027-01-13.action: Before criticising anyone today, name one fault of your own.
2027-01-13.question: Whom do I judge instead of praying for?

family.explain: Jesus told a funny story: a man with a big log in his eye wanted to take a tiny speck out of his friend's eye! Let us fix ourselves before we criticise others.
family.intention: We pray for our country's leaders.
family.ask: Ask: “Can we say something kind instead of something critical today?”

illus: A parish council in Pathanamthitta was divided by bitter criticism. The vicar asked each member to pray every day for the person they most disagreed with, by name. After three months the meetings changed. One member said: it is hard to keep judging someone you pray for every morning.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, one mediator, teach us to pray for everyone and to stop judging. Amen.
share: Prayers for everyone (1 Timothy 2:1). Whom do I leave out of my prayers?
God desires everyone to be saved (1 Timothy 2:4). Do I share this desire?
The log in your own eye (Matthew 7:3). What is my log?
pm.resp: Lord, have mercy on us all.
interc: For rulers and all in authority.
For our enemies and those we find hard to love.
For those who judge harshly, and those who are judged.
For all who do not yet know the truth.
For our group, that our prayer may be as wide as God's love.
pm.close: Father, you desire all to be saved. Make our prayer universal and our hearts merciful. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, Paul tells Timothy: I urge that supplications, prayers, intercessions, and thanksgivings be made for everyone, for kings and all who are in high positions (1 Timothy 2:1–2). Even for rulers who were persecuting Christians.

The reason: God desires everyone to be saved. There is one God; there is also one mediator between God and humankind, Christ Jesus, himself human (1 Timothy 2:4–5). Our prayer must be as wide as God's love.
Jesus warns us against judging. Why do you see the speck in your neighbor's eye, but do not notice the log in your own eye? (Matthew 7:3). We can be very sharp about others and blind about ourselves.
We cannot pray sincerely for someone and condemn him at the same time. Let us replace judgement with intercession: pray today for one person you find hard to bear. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus told a funny story about a man with a log in his eye! Before we say someone is bad, let us look at ourselves. And let us pray for everyone.

intro: Theme: “Do not judge, so that you may not be judged.”
Prayer as wide as God's will to save; judgement replaced by intercession.

q: But seek the welfare of the city where I have sent you into exile, and pray to the LORD on its behalf, for in its welfare you will find your welfare.

First of all, then, I urge that supplications, prayers, intercessions, and thanksgivings be made for everyone, for kings and all who are in high positions, so that we may lead a quiet and peaceable life in all godliness and dignity.
points.apply: Pray daily this week for our leaders by name.

sub: God desires all to be saved.
q: There is no umpire between us, who might lay his hand on us both.
For there is one God; there is also one mediator between God and humankind, Christ Jesus, himself human,
points.apply: Thank Jesus for standing between you and the Father.

q: But the LORD said to Samuel, “Do not look on his appearance or on the height of his stature, because I have rejected him; for the LORD does not see as mortals see; they look on the outward appearance, but the LORD looks on the heart.”
Why do you see the speck in your neighbor's eye, but do not notice the log in your own eye?
points.apply: Pray for the person you most often criticise.

concl: Intercession and condemnation cannot live in the same heart.
Let our prayer be as wide as God's love.
2027-01-13.resolve: Replace one criticism each day with a prayer.
